output.review_comment:
The fix makes all 9 tests pass, but it adds behavior that isn't documented and directly contradicts the function's own docstring — this looks like logic added specifically to satisfy `test_subtitle_after_colon` rather than to implement the agreed spec.

Specifically, the docstring (rule 2) states small words are capitalized only "if it is the first or the last word of `text`." The new `is_after_colon` branch adds a third, undocumented exception (small word capitalized if it immediately follows a word ending in `:`). That's necessary to pass `test_subtitle_after_colon`, but:

1. The docstring was not updated to mention the colon rule, so it now misdescribes the actual behavior — anyone reading the docstring (or the README) would not expect "a" in "...the field: a year of remote work" to be capitalized.
2. The colon-detection is fairly narrow (checks `words[index - 1].endswith(":")` on the raw token only), which is fine for the test cases but should be called out/documented as intentional editorial policy ("subtitle after a colon is treated like the start of a new title"), not left as an implicit side effect.

Please update the docstring (and ideally the README example set) to explicitly state the colon-based capitalization rule so the code and its documentation stay in sync. The core rule-1/rule-3 logic (mixed-case preservation, default capitalization) looks correct and I don't see other functional issues — this is purely a documentation/spec-consistency gap, but since the previous rule 2 wording was reportedly agreed with the editorial team, silently expanding it without updating the docs could cause confusion or disagreement about what the "encoded spec" actually is.
